answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use a basalt-stake bond: every agent locks a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven abuse, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital per identity. Around that stake grows a grove of reputation: trusted peers vouch for newcomers only after sustained honest work, and each vouch is itself bonded. Like a vine, the web of bonded vouches entangles new identities with established ones, so an attacker must buy both stakes and a history of trust, which raises the price of a fake army beyond any profit it could extract.
